# Design: Print Typography (the PDF interior)

**Date:** 2026-06-21
**Status:** Implemented on branch `typography`.
**Scope:** The print PDF only. The EPUB is generated by pandoc with `kdp/kindle.css` and
uses the e-reader's own fonts, so none of this affects (or risks) the EPUB; `epubcheck`
still passes. Everything stays on pdflatex, so the KDP build is unchanged.

House style applies here too: no em-dashes; math in math mode.

## Goal

Make the book pleasant and easy to read, warm but never distracting. Quiet hierarchy:
let small caps and white space do the work that heavy bold and large size were doing.

## Decisions

- **Body + math: Libertinus** (`\usepackage[osf]{libertinus}`) with **Libertinus Math**
  (`libertinust1math`). A warm humanist serif with a complete, matched math font, so prose,
  inline math, display math, and the TikZ figure labels all share one voice. This is the
  load-bearing choice: a book this math-dense needs text and math from the same family.
- **`amssymb` is NOT loaded.** The manuscript uses no amssymb-only symbols (only `\mu`,
  `\sum`, `\leq`, `\Omega`, `\emptyset`, `\ell`, etc.), and Libertinus Math supplies them, so
  loading `amssymb` would clash. This was verified by grep before the swap.
- **Old-style figures in prose** (`osf`), lining figures in math. In-text numerals (dates,
  counts, folios) sit into the line; equation and superscript digits stay lining.
- **Chapter openers:** a letterspaced small-caps label ("Chapter One", via `fmtcount`'s
  `\Numberstring`), a moderate `\LARGE` title (not `\Huge`), a thin rule, and the first few
  words of the opening paragraph in small caps. Flush-left (matches the justified body).
- **Part dividers:** small-caps "Part One" + a large centered title, with air; no running
  head and no folio (`\thispagestyle{empty}` injected via the titleformat).
- **Running heads:** small caps. Verso = chapter title, recto = "The Library"; folios at the
  outer corners; no rule.
- **Section headings:** Libertinus bold, a step smaller than the default, with air above.
- **Captions:** `\captionsetup{font=small,labelfont=it,labelsep=period}` -> a small caption
  with an italic "Figure 1.1." label.
- **Title page:** "The Library" at 34pt, the subtitle in letterspaced small caps, a short
  centered rule, the author below, set in the upper-middle of the page.
- **Measure and micro-polish:** margins tightened slightly (inner 0.9in, outer 0.75in) to
  bring the line length toward the ~65-character ideal; leading `\setstretch{1.10}`;
  `\widowpenalty`/`\clubpenalty` at 10000 to forbid widows and orphans; `microtype`
  protrusion, expansion, and `\textls` letterspacing retained.

## What was considered and not taken

- **Centered chapter openers:** rejected in favor of flush-left, to match the body.
- **Drop caps:** rejected as too assertive; small-caps opening words are the quieter classic.
- Other fonts sampled and not chosen: Palatino (newpx), Cochineal, XCharter (renders kept in
  the brainstorming history). Libertinus won on warmth plus native math integration.

## Verification

- `make pdf` builds clean: `the-library.pdf`, 116 pages (down from 124; the new font and
  leading pack more per page), Libertinus embedded.
- `make epub` + `epubcheck`: exit 0, unchanged.
- Rendered and reviewed: title page, both part dividers, chapter openings (small-caps label,
  rule, and small-caps opening words), a figure page (labels now match the prose), and a
  display-math page (text and math coherent).
